title: Bram and the Archive
premise: Tamsin Brightwater, the last caretaker of a terraforming garden seeded for colonists who never arrived, discovers their lonely beacon is actually a receiver for a signal that predates human settlement. When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the system, Tamsin learns the flicker was a countdown: something in dead space is waking, and the Archive — a derelict relay holding records of every crime committed during the colony's founding — has begun broadcasting its evidence. Hunted by the Charter fleet that wants the Archive silenced, Tamsin joins a ragged crew of outcasts and races to the relay, choosing between destroying the truth that could save them and delivering it to a system not ready to hear it. In the end, Tamsin broadcasts the Archive openly, sacrificing the beacon and the garden's last seed-vault, and finds that justice, once released, belongs to everyone.
about_author: Rosalind Iversen is a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote research stations before turning to fiction. She writes about people who keep things running long after anyone remembers why.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Establishes the garden, the unclaimed beacon, and Tamsin's quiet devotion to unborn colonists. Gravity flickers; instruments scream; the beacon answers something. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by wonder and dread.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Tamsin surveys damage after the flicker, finding plants growing in patterns they shouldn't — guided by the beacon's new signal. A scavenger ship lands uninvited. Emotional beat: protective anger at strangers trespassing on sacred ground.

chapters.title: Crew of the Long Odds
chapters.summary: Introduces the scavengers: ex-Charter pilot Ovid, engineer Sefa, and mute navigator Wren, all fugitives. They reveal the nine-second event hit every station. Tamsin bargains passage using knowledge of the signal. Emotional beat: wary first trust.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Tamsin decodes the beacon's logs: it was built to receive from the Archive, a pre-colony relay in dead space. The signal is a broadcast beginning. Ovid recognizes Charter fleet signatures inbound. Emotional beat: the past is not what Tamsin believed.

chapters.title: Departure Protocol
chapters.summary: Tamsin seals the garden, taking only a seed-vault, and burns remaining supplies into the soil as an offering. The fleet arrives as they lift off. POV shifts briefly to a Charter captain, Vess, ordered to erase the signal's source. Emotional beat: grief disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: Aboard the ship, tensions flare over course and cargo. Sefa teaches Tamsin the engines; Wren communicates through drawn star-charts that eerily match the Archive's coordinates. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The First Interception
chapters.summary: A Charter patrol corners them at a fuel depot. Ovid flies a suicidal slingshot through debris while Tamsin spoofs their transponder using beacon codes. Emotional beat: terror transformed into competence; Tamsin stops being cargo.

chapters.title: Vess
chapters.summary: Captain Vess's POV. She interrogates survivors of the depot and realizes the Archive contains her own family's crimes from the founding era. Her orders harden; her conscience fractures. Emotional beat: the hunter begins to doubt.

chapters.title: Signal Growing Louder
chapters.summary: The Archive's broadcast intensifies, causing systems across the ship to echo fragments: names, verdicts, confessions. Wren reacts violently — the fragments include her birth-station's destruction. Emotional beat: history as wound.

chapters.title: The Graveyard Belt
chapters.summary: They cross a belt of scuttled colony ships, evidence of the founding purge the Archive recorded. Tamsin realizes the 'unborn colonists' were never coming because they were killed. Emotional beat: faith shattered into purpose.

chapters.title: Mutiny Weather
chapters.summary: Ovid wants to sell the Archive's location to the highest bidder rather than reach it; Sefa and Wren side with Tamsin. A storm of ionized debris forces them to cooperate mid-crisis. Emotional beat: conflict without villains, only fear.

chapters.title: Halfway House
chapters.summary: They dock at an outlaw station to repair. Tamsin meets archivists-in-exile who have spent decades collecting testimony. They offer maps but warn: broadcasting the Archive means every guilty party hunts you forever. Emotional beat: justice has a price tag.

chapters.title: The Price Named Aloud
chapters.summary: Tamsin weighs the cost: the garden dies without them; the seed-vault may be their only legacy. Ovid confesses his own entry exists in the Archive. He chooses to continue anyway. Emotional beat: redemption chosen knowingly.

chapters.title: Fleet at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Her squadron reaches the edge of dead space first and receives direct orders to destroy the relay regardless of contents. She stalls, buying time she can't explain. Emotional beat: disobedience as the first act of courage.

chapters.title: Through the Silence
chapters.summary: The crew runs the silent corridor where no signal escapes — comms die, Wren's charts become their only eyes. Tamsin holds the seed-vault through a hull breach scare. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in absolute isolation.

chapters.title: The Archive Itself
chapters.summary: They arrive: the relay is vast, ancient, older than the colony — it recorded the founders' arrival and everything buried since. The broadcast was a distress call from the machine's failing core. Emotional beat: awe curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: Everything True
chapters.summary: Tamsin reads the full record: the founders' massacre, the erased colonies, the reason the beacon was orphaned. Vess arrives demanding surrender; instead Tamsin shows her her family's name. Emotional beat: confrontation becomes witness.

chapters.title: The Choice of Fire
chapters.summary: Charter command orders Vess to burn the relay. She refuses, turning her guns on her own squadron's lead ship. Ovid sacrifices himself covering the relay's antenna array so the broadcast can complete. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Tamsin keys the transmission: the entire Archive, unredacted, to every receiver in the system — including the beacon in the garden, now singing to the living instead of the unborn. Emotional beat: release; the truth leaves their hands forever.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: The system convulses: stations riot, tribunals form spontaneously, Charter fractures. Vess surrenders herself as first witness. Sefa and Wren choose to stay with the Archive and maintain it. Emotional beat: justice begins, unfinished.

chapters.title: Seeds in Old Ground
chapters.summary: Tamsin returns to the ruined garden, expecting nothing, and finds settlers — real ones, drawn by the broadcast — already planting in the disturbed soil. They ask Tamsin to stay and teach. Emotional beat: the garden finally has its people.

chapters.title: Bram and the Archive
chapters.summary: Tamsin's final POV, years later: the beacon rebuilt as a public library-relay, the Archive maintained by volunteers, Bram — the name Tamsin gives the first tree grown from the vault — shading children born free of the old lies. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory kept alive.
